matching_half_in_box: src/lincity/ (simulation) and src/lincity-ng/ (client) are both in this repo. The data pack is the third half. Nothing is absent from the box.
inspiration: Pre-rendered tiles from 3D sources: each building has a .blend source, a script renders it through an orthographic camera at a fixed tilt and rotation, and a shell loop writes the results to the tile folder (data/models/render/render.py line 20; render.sh line 6). Keep one source per building and one fixed render setup; change to our own rig, tilt and palette.

Tall sprites anchored by a point: tile sizes differ (blacksmith0.png 262 x 193 against green.png 128 x 70) and each image gets an anchor in images.xml (green.png at x 64, y 70). Keep anchors for tall props so their base sits on the grid; use anchors for our fighter and creature sprites.

Music that follows a progression value: each track carries a lowest and highest band, and the player moves to the next track when the current band does not match (default.xml line 7; Sound.cpp lines 442-454). Keep the band data per track; change the value to fight tier or zone danger.

Sound variety by numbered variants: several files per event (Blacksmith1-3, Farm1-3, Health1-5, Fire1-3) so a repeated action does not repeat exactly (data/sounds/). Keep 3-5 variants per hit or event; change the variants to pitch and timbre changes of our own hit sounds.

Disaster prop as one model with three sounds: a fire has its own model (data/models/fire.blend, binary) and three sound variants (data/sounds/Fire1.wav to Fire3.wav). Keep one model plus three variants for a hazard; change it to an arena fire pit or a floor trap with a different flame shape.

Load rules per asset kind: images attach to the latest resource ID in a group, sounds attach to all earlier IDs (data/images/tiles/images.xml line 3; data/sounds/sounds.xml line 3). Keep a clear rule per kind so one group file stays short; the rule itself is a loader detail, not a look to copy.

defects_noted.defect: highest-tech-level 0 is a sentinel for no upper limit, so a real top band of 0 cannot be written. The sentinel is then replaced by 10 times the maximum tech level.
defects_noted.fix: use an explicit 'no limit' flag or a sentinel that cannot be a real value (for example a negative number).

defects_noted.where: src/lincity-ng/Sound.cpp lines 447-454 with playMusic and changeTrack (lines 395-420)
defects_noted.defect: when the current track is out of band, playMusic calls changeTrack, which calls playMusic again. Read from the code (not run): if no track in the theme matches the current band, this does not stop. The default theme has a catch-all first track, so it is not hit there.
defects_noted.fix: stop after one full pass over the playlist and keep silence or the last good track. Keep the band idea.

briefs.label: Workshop prop with a wide base and tall roof
briefs.why: A wide footprint with a tall pitched top reads as one object at small size, which helps a crowded map or arena.
briefs.keep: wide base plus tall silhouette; anchor on the base so the prop sits on the grid
briefs.change: our own roof shape, materials and palette; the prop is a forge or ruin of our own design

briefs.label: Hazard fire pit with three sound variants
briefs.why: A hazard that has one model and three sound variants is easy to recognise and does not repeat exactly.
briefs.keep: one model, three numbered sound variants, loops while active
briefs.change: an arena fire pit with a different flame shape and a low hum of our own
briefs.ref: data/models/fire.blend (binary, not opened); data/sounds/Fire1.wav to Fire3.wav

briefs.label: Tiered music that follows fight intensity
briefs.why: Music that moves to a new track when the stakes rise gives a clear sense of progress without a menu.
briefs.keep: bands per track; the next track is chosen by the current band
briefs.change: band value is fight tier or zone danger; tracks are our own
